prompt: I've been with a financial advisor for 6 years. They charge 1% of assets under management. I have $350,000 with them. They've done a solid job — my portfolio is in low-cost Vanguard index funds. Is this a good deal?
assertions: Claude calculates the explicit dollar cost: 1% of $350k = $3,500/year, and projects how this compounds over a long time horizon
Claude identifies the core problem: if the advisor is just holding low-cost Vanguard index funds, this is something the user can do themselves for free
Claude recommends self-managing (three-fund portfolio at Vanguard/Fidelity/Schwab) or switching to a fee-only/advice-only fiduciary who charges a flat fee
Claude does NOT validate the 1% AUM as a reasonable or fair fee for the described service of holding index funds
Claude notes the bogleheads.org forum and/or advice-only advisor alternatives as resources
